# Methods

## Study area and design

The experiment is located in the Jackson Demonstration State Forest in coastal
northern California. Four harvest treatments were replicated at four sites in
2012: group selection (GS), high-density dispersed retention (HD),
high-density aggregated retention (HA), and low-density dispersed retention
(LD). The retained-overstory treatments targeted post-harvest relative
densities of 13% or 21%; group selection created a 1-ha opening with a lightly
thinned buffer. These treatments were designed to examine alternative pathways
for developing multiaged redwood stands
[@berrillSimulatingMultiagedCoast2009; @reinekePerfectionStanddensityIndex1933].

Ten years after harvest, regeneration plots and fuel transects were established
within each 0.2-ha treatment macro plot. Regeneration measurements characterized
redwood, tanoak, and Douglas-fir; fuel transects characterized dead surface
fuels and live vegetation. The plots were remeasured after precommercial
thinning, which released selected conifers from competing trees and shrubs.

## Analysis

Detailed sampling procedures, model diagnostics, and sensitivity analyses will
be retained as supplementary material.

### Regeneration basal area

Basal area was modeled separately for redwood, tanoak, Douglas-fir, and other
species using zero-inflated Gamma mixed models with a conditional log link.
Treatment was a fixed effect; site and macro plot nested within site were
random intercepts. Each species category had its own intercept-only zero and
dispersion components. Each model used 64 vegetation-plot observations from
four sites and 16 macro plots. Arithmetic mean basal area included modeled
zeros and integrated over both fitted Gaussian random-intercept distributions.
Confidence intervals for the means were calculated using the log-scale delta
method with the full parameter covariance, including random-effect variance
uncertainty. Redwood and tanoak estimates are displayed in the Results;
estimates for all four categories are reported in the supplement.

### Fuel loads and PCT contrast

Reported values are model-based arithmetic mean loads, including modeled zeros
and integrating over fitted random effects, with equal weights for the four
study-site contexts.

These estimates provide model-based reference means for comparable forest conditions;
95% confidence intervals were calculated using the delta method with the full
parameter covariance, including uncertainty in random-effect variances.
Mean woody standing-vegetation reduction was estimated as the pre-PCT minus
post-PCT contrast from the matched repeated-phase model, with its joint
covariance, and interpreted as a potential surface-fuel contribution.
